claims.statement: install.InstallNative is the single host-neutral installation engine: it validates shared inputs, resolves the stable root, discovers the skill list once, and delegates all concrete writes to port.HostInstaller implementations (Name() + Install(request)); the composition root harnessapp passes exactly codex.NewInstaller, claude.NewInstaller, and omo.NewInstaller, so the aggregate result covers hosts in the deterministic order codex → claude → omo with per-host failures joined into the final result.

Default install writes only user-level config (skill symlinks, MCP registration, SessionStart hook) and creates nothing inside a target repository; repo-local files (.claude/skills, .mcp.json, .omo/skills, .omo/mcp.json) are created only when --project-local is explicitly passed, and the contract matrix asserts their absence otherwise.

Each host adapter owns exactly its own user-level surfaces: Codex writes ~/.codex/skills/* symlinks, the [mcp_servers.agent_harness] block in ~/.codex/config.toml, and the SessionStart hook in ~/.codex/hooks.json; Claude Code writes ~/.claude/skills/* symlinks, the user-scope agent_harness MCP server in ~/.claude.json, and the SessionStart hook in ~/.claude/settings.json; Omo writes ~/.omo/agent/skills/* symlinks, agent_harness in ~/.omo/mcp.json, and the lifecycle extension ~/.omo/extensions/agent-harness.js.

Each installer also refreshes the repo-owned host templates under configs/ (configs/codex/mcp.config.toml and hooks.json, configs/claude/mcp.project.json and hooks.settings.json, configs/omo/mcp.json and agent-harness.js) so the checked-in templates cannot drift from the content the installer writes into user homes.

Before delegating, install.DefaultNativeInstallRequest normalizes the request: ResolveStableNativeRoot maps a linked Git worktree to the source checkout owning the common .git directory, ValidateStableNativeRuntime rejects binaries outside that stable root so installed hooks always execute an installer-owned binary, CodexHome defaults to ~/.codex (overridable via CODEX_HOME), and the skill list is derived from skills/<name>/SKILL.md directories, deduplicated and sorted.

skills/ is the single host-neutral source of truth for shared skills (34 SKILL.md directories: 12 pioneer namesakes fixed by internal/domain/pioneerskill plus operational skills); installation links each host's user skill directory to <checkout>/skills/<name> via symlinks and never copies content, so host-local copies that drift from skills/ are forbidden drift.

Skill linking honors a per-skill install.json host filter ({"hosts":[...]} enables a skill only for listed hosts; missing or invalid config keeps the historical default of all hosts, with skips reported as messages) and prunes stale harness-owned symlinks: PruneStaleSkillLinks removes only links pointing under this checkout's skills/ whose target no longer exists, leaves foreign links, resolving links, and non-symlinks untouched, and reports would_remove during dry-run.

Default installs register exactly one hook event, SessionStart, for both Codex (~/.codex/hooks.json) and Claude Code (~/.claude/settings.json), invoking the shared context CLI ('<bin>' hook session-start --host codex|claude) with a 5-second timeout; this is because both Claude Code 2.1.247 and codex-cli 0.150.1 re-run SessionStart with source "compact" after compaction and only SessionStart output can carry model-facing additionalContext, while PostCompact output is user-display-only, so PostCompact is not registered and upgrades remove any managed PostCompact group while preserving non-harness groups.

The hook CLI exposes only two subcommands — hook session-start and hook post-compact — and both merely read the static project-doc catalog and emit host-compatible JSON; they never touch IssueOps, lifecycle reminders, runtime state, telemetry, SQLite, worker recovery, or durable state, and hook output is neither an enforcement path nor ownership evidence. post-compact stays available for Omo (whose session_compact has no SessionStart re-run) and diagnosis; HARNESS_DISABLE_HOOKS=1 turns registered hooks into silent no-ops.

Host hook rendering differences are isolated in internal/domain/hook adapters: Claude Code separates the user-visible systemMessage from model-facing hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext, while Codex renders additionalContext in its TUI so the readable user view replaces the compact string and systemMessage is never emitted; with nothing to inject both hosts receive {}.

Hook and MCP registration is a merge, never an overwrite: installers read existing JSON, fail closed on malformed known hook events, replace only agent-harness-owned groups on known lifecycle events while preserving third-party groups and their order, delete the obsolete hyphenated agent-harness MCP alias, and merge agent_harness into the existing server maps (Claude ~/.claude.json and Omo ~/.omo/mcp.json, both mode 0600).

Codex config.toml is edited conservatively — backed up once as config.toml.harness.bak, stripped only of harness-owned mcp_servers.agent_harness sections, canonical block appended with HARNESS_ROOT, written mode 0600 — and installers emit two drift diagnostics: HookTargetDriftMessages for installer-owned hooks whose executable path no longer matches the canonical binary, and HookTargetGenerationMessages for the same-path-different-build-generation case (#328) including an exact recovery command.

Installation commits as a staged activation transaction: a dry-run preflight runs first, Begin persists a pending transition with a transition ID and candidate binary SHA-256, install then applies host writes, and Seal requires strict readback of exactly six evidences — mcp and hooks surfaces for each of codex, claude, and omo — each carrying a semantic SHA-256 of the expected surface plus filesystem identity (regular single-link file, device/inode/mode, re-stat during read); Claude and Omo readbacks additionally reject the obsolete hyphenated alias and Omo compares extension bytes exactly. Any host-write or seal failure rolls back snapshots and aborts the transition.

Before applying any host write the installer snapshots every affected file, symlink, mode, and newly created parent directory (installHostTransaction); on failure it restores them in reverse order — including removing created parents and restoring original symlink targets or file bytes — and, when the failure happened during a seal step, marks abort_required so the pending activation transition can be recovered.

scripts/install-native.sh owns the staged binary activation: it builds the candidate into a staged temp file, verifies it, runs the dry-run preflight and activation begin, fsyncs the staged file and atomically os.replace()s it onto bin/agent-harness, then runs the seal-step install; a test pins that the script must order staged begin → atomic replace → canonical seal, and on exit without commit the EXIT trap aborts the transition with the SHA-256-verified binary.

configs/upstream.json is a declarative, currently Claude-only catalog of optional third-party plugins and Git skills (four plugins plus cua-driver) that install/update provisions when missing; provisioning runs only after the native activation receipt is sealed, is capped at five minutes, and never changes install success — every outcome including total sync failure is recorded as an 'upstream ...' message while the harness install stays ok, and an unconfigured SyncUpstream dependency skips upstream entirely.

Upstream planning is a pure domain decision: declared entries already present on the host are skipped (a plugin counts when 'claude plugin list --json' reports name@marketplace in any scope; a skill counts when ~/.claude/skills/<name> exists, whoever created it), and when the claude CLI is absent plugin entries become skips with reason 'host plugin CLI is unavailable' rather than failures — an unavailable host is a skip, never an install failure.

Upstream provisioning treats executing the Claude CLI as a write: with --dry-run the service reports declared plugins as planned without spawning the CLI at all — not even to read its inventory — because the claude binary creates $HOME/.claude and $HOME/.claude.json on startup, which previously made install --dry-run mutate the home directory it was only describing; skills stay observed because that is a side-effect-free directory read.

Upstream skills are fetched with a shallow sparse git clone into a harness-owned cache at <state dir>/upstream/skills/<name> and symlinked into ~/.claude/skills/<name>, mirroring first-party link shape; a fetched directory without SKILL.md is rejected leaving neither cache copy nor link, only a symlink is ever replaced at the host path, and because the cache lives outside skills/ the stale-link prune never touches upstream links.

External tools are never native-install dependencies: install, update, self-verify, and IssueOps readiness must reproduce on machines with none of them present, enforced mechanically by TestInstallNativeScriptDoesNotWireCompanionTools (which fails if scripts/install-native.sh regains any companion-tool installer path such as claude-mem, agentmemory, llm-wiki, codegraph, or npm-based installers) and by the Omo ADR forbidding the external Omo runtime as an install prerequisite or readiness gate.

Adding a host is deliberately narrow: implement port.HostInstaller in a new internal/adapter/<host> package planning user-level surfaces through shared installutil primitives (plan accumulator, WriteTextPlan/WriteJSONPlan, EnsureSymlinkPlan, PlanHostSkillLinks, hook merge helpers, activation evidence capture), then wire it only in the composition root — append the installer to the InstallNative closure, add its VerifyActivation readback to hostActivationReadback, and inject the package's function-variable dependencies. Domain/application policy must never be duplicated per host, cross-adapter imports are banned (the dependency ratchet allows concrete-adapter edges only from cmd/harness/harnessapp), and un-injected dependencies fail closed (e.g. 'native installer is not configured').

The setup surface has three entry commands plus two scripts: agent-harness install with --interactive/--project-local/--path-mode/--adopt-command-file/--dry-run/--json is the canonical installer; agent-harness update and bootstrap locate scripts/install-native.sh, forward those flags plus --skip-build, and after a non-dry-run run refresh the shared daemon (daemon stop then daemon start with the installed binary) without ever running git pull; ./install.sh builds bin/agent-harness and execs agent-harness install, adding --interactive automatically in an interactive terminal with no arguments.

--interactive requires a terminal and prompts for project-local opt-in and PATH mode (warning that most installs should keep project-local disabled); --dry-run plans every file and link without writing — results expose WouldWrite/WouldCreate entries, no paths are created (asserted by TestNativeInstallDryRunDoesNotWrite), and the upstream path must not even spawn the claude CLI.

--path-mode controls the command shims ~/.local/bin/agent-harness and the managed ah shorthand: auto (default) also appends a marked export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" line to the preferred shell rc when ~/.local/bin is not already on PATH; manual and skip create the shims but leave the rc alone. ah is a symlink, not a wrapper — install refuses to replace a regular-file or foreign-targeted ah, and replacing an existing regular file at ~/.local/bin/agent-harness requires --adopt-command-file, admitted only for binaries matching the static Go build identity and executed as a transaction with a 0600 backup, atomic exchange, and pre-seal rollback.

--sync is not part of the host-install flag set: the only state-changing --sync is agent-harness project bootstrap --sync, which refreshes a target repo's operating docs and profile metadata; the update/bootstrap flag set defines --project-local, --dry-run, --path-mode, --interactive, --json, and --skip-build but no --sync flag, even though the golden usage text still advertises [--sync] on the bootstrap line.

Project-local surfaces are asymmetric by design: Claude Code gets .claude/skills/* links plus .mcp.json under the server name agent_harness_project (avoiding scope collision with user-scope agent_harness) but never a repo-local .claude/settings.json because Claude project-local hooks are committable; Omo gets .omo/skills/* plus .omo/mcp.json; Codex has no project-local surface at all.

The Omo installer embeds the SHA-256 of the currently advertised MCP tool catalog into the server env as HARNESS_MCP_CATALOG_SHA256, because Omo reuses a tools/list schema keyed by its server-config hash for up to ~7 days: changing the catalog changes the config hash and forces the next session to re-fetch tools. The value is a cache revision token only and does not steer MCP handler behavior; a missing or empty digest fails the Omo MCP config write.

~/.omo/extensions/agent-harness.js maps Omo session_start and accepted session_compact events to agent-harness hook session-start --json and hook post-compact --json, injecting the compact project-doc payload as a hidden custom message with triggerTurn:false; hook failures surface as UI warnings and never abort the session, and the extension byte content is exactly verified during activation readback.

Install health is observable without re-running the installer: agent-harness inspect reports Codex/Claude skill install paths, MCP configuration, and project-local state; live checks are per-host file tests plus codex mcp get agent_harness / claude mcp list, and hook behavior can be smoke-tested by piping {"cwd":...,"source":"compact"} into agent-harness hook session-start --host codex; doctor diagnoses install, state, hooks, MCP, daemon, and project docs together.

The install surface is pinned by TestNativeInstallAdapterContractMatrix, which runs user-global and project-local cases through all three installers, asserts semantic invariants (deterministic host order, sorted skill names, symlinks resolving under $ROOT/skills/*, SessionStart-only hooks with removed lifecycle events absent, exact MCP config content, no repo-local writes by default), and goldens the full normalized plan into internal/adapter/testdata/native_install_contract_matrix.golden.json; a standalone install dry-run smoke (temporary HOME/CODEX_HOME/HARNESS_ROOT) plus scripts/release-repro-smoke.sh verify no-write dry runs on clean machines.
